name: Operate gas units around the clock
summary: Crews of certified power engineers run the converted gas-fired steam units around the clock on rotating 12-hour shifts. In each plant-shift the crew takes over from the previous shift, follows the dispatch targets passed on by the real-time desk, watches the unit on the control system, walks rounds, runs routine tests, isolates equipment for maintenance, answers alarms and writes up defects, then hands over. The work is slow to learn and error-prone at the handover, during alarms and when the unit trips; since the units became merchant gas units they change load and cycle more often, which adds alarms, ramps and wear.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator running three coal units converted to gas-fired steam (about 400 to 460 MW each) on two plant sites.
baseline.notes: One case is one plant-shift: two plant sites (one with two units) times two 12-hour shifts a day gives about 122 a month. In 2019-2020 the units still burned coal, with coal handling and ash crews not shown here.

unit_of_work: one plant-shift (12 hours of one plant site's operating crew)
trigger: A 12-hour shift begins at the plant site (06:00 or 18:00), with dispatch instructions arriving from the real-time desk through it.
end_state: The shift log is signed, timesheets are entered, unit status is sent and the next crew has taken over; or the unit has tripped and the crew has moved into the forced outage response.

volume.seasonality: Constant: every day has two shifts per plant site. Workload inside a shift rises in winter cold snaps and price spikes, when units cycle and trip more.

evidence.note: Two plant sites times two shifts times 29 to 31 days, matching the organisation file.
ABSA certificate needed to supervise a plant (ALIS); one supervisor per plant site per shift on a five-crew rotation is about 10 people; the organisation file lists 12.
About two operators per plant-shift on a five-crew rotation (about 20 to 22 FTE); the organisation file lists 45, which fits the coal era.

roles.title: Field operator (third- or fourth-class power engineer)

evidence.note: About 3 to 4 field operators per plant-shift on a five-crew rotation (about 32 to 36 FTE); the organisation file lists 55.
Calls to the plant and restatements during derates; most desk work is in mkt-respond-dispatch and mkt-restate-offers. Not listed in the organisation file's roles for this process.

systems.name: AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)
Energy trading and risk management system
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Document management and engineering drawings repository

resources.name: Gas-fired steam unit converted from coal (about 400 to 460 MW)

steps.name: Hold pre-shift safety meeting
steps.description: The shift supervisor gathers the incoming crew in the control room before relief, reads out the hazards of the day (open permits, equipment out of service, weather, any start or stop planned), assigns rounds and checks everyone is fit for duty. Each person signs the meeting record.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 2 hazard assessment, applied as a pre-shift hazard review

evidence.note: Person-minutes for a crew of about 6 to 7 people meeting for 10 to 20 minutes; common practice at Alberta thermal plants.

steps.name: Take over the control room
steps.description: The incoming control room operators read the outgoing shift log, the DCS alarm summary and the list of equipment out of service, and talk through the dispatch target, any derates and abnormal settings with the operators they relieve. They sign the log to accept the unit.

error.defect_description: An abnormal condition or bypassed alarm is not passed on at handover.

control.basis: Site shift turnover procedure: written log and verbal handover before relief

evidence.note: Daily operating log and monitoring duties from ALIS; minutes are an estimate for about two operators.

steps.name: Walk down the plant with the outgoing field operators
steps.description: Each incoming field operator meets the operator they relieve on their area (boiler, turbine hall, water treatment and balance of plant) and walks past equipment running abnormally, tagged out or under repair, noting anything to watch.

evidence.note: About 3 to 4 field operators per plant-shift, 15 to 30 minutes each.

steps.name: Review the shift plan
steps.description: The shift supervisor reviews the log, open permits and lockouts, the maintenance work planned for the shift, the gas nomination and any pipeline notices, the latest water chemistry results and the emissions monitor status, and decides the order of work for the crew.

evidence.note: Supervisor practice at multi-unit thermal plants; minutes estimated.

steps.name: Confirm unit capability with the real-time desk
steps.description: The real-time trader on shift calls the plant, confirms the available capability, ramp rate and minimum stable level the desk has offered for each unit, and tells the supervisor what dispatches to expect from the merit order for the next hours.

error.defect_description: Capability offered does not match what the plant can deliver.

evidence.note: The company manages its own offers and dispatch is by AESO merit order; call content and minutes estimated.

steps.name: Follow dispatch instructions
steps.description: Through the shift the control room operator receives each new dispatch for the unit from the real-time desk, acknowledges it and sets the unit load demand on the DCS so the unit starts moving within 10 minutes and ramps at the offered rate.

error.defect_description: Wrong MW target or late ramp, giving a dispatch compliance deviation.

control.basis: AESO ISO rule 203.4 s.4 (begin ramping within 10 minutes of the dispatch time)

evidence.note: 10-minute start of ramp from the rule; number of dispatches per shift (about 2 to 8 per unit) estimated.

steps.name: Monitor and control the unit from the DCS
steps.description: The control room operators watch drum level, steam pressure and temperature, furnace pressure, burner flames, turbine vibration and emissions on the DCS screens, adjust setpoints and switch loops to manual when automatic control misbehaves, and coordinate the field operators by radio.

evidence.note: Monitoring and manual control duties from ALIS; two operators for most of a 12-hour shift is an estimate.

steps.name: Do the first field rounds
steps.description: Each field operator walks a fixed route through the boiler, turbine, condensate and feedwater, cooling water and gas supply areas, reads local gauges and tank levels, listens for leaks and abnormal noise, and checks lube oil and seal systems on running pumps and fans.

error.defect_description: A slow leak or rising bearing temperature is missed on the round.

evidence.note: Rounds of about 2 hours each for 3 to 4 field operators; route length estimated for a converted 400 MW unit.

steps.name: Record the round readings
steps.description: The field operators type the readings from their round sheets or handhelds into the operating log and data historian and flag any reading outside its normal band for the control room.

error.defect_description: Reading keyed wrongly or abnormal value not flagged.

evidence.note: Daily log duty from ALIS; minutes estimated.

steps.name: Run routine tests and equipment changeovers
steps.description: Field operators carry out the shift's scheduled tests and changeovers: rotating standby pumps and fans, testing the fire pumps and emergency lube oil pump, blowing down level gauges and checking burner and igniter condition.

evidence.note: Operator routine duties; frequency and minutes estimated.

steps.name: Adjust chemical feed to the water chemistry results
steps.description: A field operator reads the latest results from the chemistry technician and adjusts the boiler chemical feed pumps and continuous blowdown to bring pH, phosphate or oxygen scavenger back into the ranges set in the chemistry procedure.

next.condition: day shift with maintenance work needing isolation

evidence.note: Common practice at drum boiler plants; minutes estimated.

steps.name: Isolate equipment for maintenance crews
steps.description: For each permit request approved for the shift, a field operator closes and locks valves and breakers on the isolation list, hangs locks and tags, and proves zero energy with the maintenance worker before the permit is handed over.

error.defect_description: Isolation point missed or wrong valve locked.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15 control of hazardous energy (lockout)

evidence.note: Isolation and lockout duty from ALIS; share of shifts and minutes estimated. Permit issue itself is in gas-issue-work-permits.

steps.name: Respond to alarms
steps.description: The control room operator acknowledges each DCS alarm, reads the trend behind it and decides whether it is a nuisance, something to watch, a fault for a field operator to check, or a unit upset that needs immediate action.

next.condition: a fault needs a field check
alarms cleared from the control room
unit trips or must be derated

evidence.note: Alarm load and split estimated; about 0.1 forced outage or derate per plant-shift follows from about 12 a month over 122 plant-shifts.

steps.name: Check the fault in the field
steps.description: A field operator goes to the equipment named by the alarm, looks for leaks, trips or failed instruments, resets what can be reset under the operating procedure and reports back by radio.

evidence.note: Common operator practice; split estimated.

steps.name: Raise a work request
steps.description: The control room operator writes a work request in the maintenance module of the ERP with the equipment tag, symptom and priority, so the maintenance planner and supervisor see it in the next morning's review.

error.defect_description: Wrong equipment tag or vague symptom, so the planner has to ask again.

evidence.note: Notification practice in plant maintenance systems; minutes estimated.

steps.name: Do the second field rounds
steps.description: Late in the shift the field operators repeat their rounds, compare readings with the first round and pay extra attention to equipment flagged earlier, isolated equipment and anything the control room asked them to watch.

evidence.note: Second round per 12-hour shift is an estimate.

steps.name: Check emissions against the approval limits
steps.description: The control room operator checks the emissions monitor readings for NOx and the monitor's own health and calibration status, and tells the supervisor if a rolling average is approaching its limit or the monitor is out of service.

control.basis: EPEA approval emission limits and Alberta CEMS Code

evidence.note: Plant practice; release share estimated.

steps.name: Declare the trip or derate to the desk
steps.description: The shift supervisor calls the real-time desk to say the unit has tripped or must run below its offered capability, gives the MW now available and the expected duration, and opens the forced outage response.

next.condition: unit tripped; crew moves to the forced outage response
unit stays on line at reduced output

evidence.note: Rule needs a restatement within 20 minutes of a deviation of 20 minutes or more; trip versus derate split estimated.

steps.name: Restate the unit's available capability
steps.description: The real-time trader enters the reduced available capability for the unit in the Energy Trading System with the reason, which removes the top offer blocks from the merit order until the unit is restated back up.

error.defect_description: Wrong MW or wrong hours restated.

control.basis: AESO ISO rule 203.4 s.5 (restate within 20 minutes of an operational deviation)

next.condition: continue the shift at reduced output

evidence.note: 20-minute deadline and effect on offer blocks from the rule and information document.

steps.name: Report a spill or release
steps.description: When a chemical, oil or water release or an emissions exceedance happens on shift, the shift supervisor stops it where safe, records what, where and how much in the incident and environmental system, and phones the environment specialist who decides whether the regulator must be told.

control.basis: EPEA release reporting duty, applied through the company incident procedure

evidence.note: Release share and minutes estimated.

steps.name: Complete the shift log and timesheets
steps.description: The shift supervisor finishes the shift log (dispatches, trips, alarms, work requests, permits and readings out of band), enters crew hours and overtime in the time and attendance system and signs the log.

error.defect_description: Overtime or callout hours entered wrongly.

evidence.note: Daily log duty from ALIS; timesheet practice and minutes estimated.

steps.name: Send end-of-shift unit status
steps.description: The shift supervisor emails the real-time desk, the forecasting analyst, the chemistry technician and the emissions team a short unit status: MW capability, equipment out of service, derates expected and work planned on the next shift.

error.defect_description: Capability in the status note differs from what the desk has offered.

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes estimated.

steps.name: Hand over to the next crew
steps.description: The outgoing control room operators brief the incoming crew on dispatch, alarms, isolations and open work, answer their questions and leave once the relief has signed the log.

evidence.note: Outgoing side of the turnover; minutes estimated.

exceptions.name: Unit trip during the shift
exceptions.description: The unit trips; the supervisor declares it to the desk and the crew moves into the forced outage response, so the normal second rounds and end-of-shift steps happen inside that process.

exceptions.name: Derate restated and run through
exceptions.description: Equipment trouble forces the unit below its offered capability; the desk restates the capability in ETS within 20 minutes and the crew runs the rest of the shift at reduced output.

exceptions.name: Spill or release
exceptions.description: An oil, chemical or water release or an emissions exceedance is contained and written up for the environment team.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from start of shift to completed handover
benchmarks.population: One 12-hour shift plus about 15 to 30 minutes of overlap at each end

evidence.note: A plant-shift lasts 12 hours by definition; the overlap is common practice. The simulator adds every person-minute in sequence, so its cycle time is much longer than this; see assumptions.

benchmarks.unit: people on shift at one plant site
benchmarks.population: Converted gas-fired steam units of about 400 MW, one or two units per site

evidence.note: Estimate: one ABSA-certified shift supervisor, one to three control room operators and three to four field operators. Coal-era crews were larger.
About 12 forced outages or derates a month (organisation file estimate for gas-respond-forced-outage) over about 122 plant-shifts, rounded down because some start during start-ups.

pain_points.description: Handover quality depends on what the outgoing operator remembers to say; bypassed alarms and temporary settings get lost between crews.

evidence.note: Common finding in shift-work reviews; not measured for this organisation.

pain_points.description: More frequent load changes and starts since the units became merchant gas units add alarms, ramps and thermal stress, and cycling is linked to tube and header failures.

evidence.note: Cycling damage from the cited NETL and Intertek work; optimisation toward high-price hours from the TransAlta report.

pain_points.description: Round readings are written on paper and typed in later, so a reading out of band can sit unnoticed for hours.

evidence.note: Common at plants of this age in 2019-2022; estimate.

pain_points.description: A derate must be restated within 20 minutes, but it depends on the supervisor reaching the desk quickly by phone.

evidence.note: 20-minute restatement deadline from the rule.

sources.title: Power engineer: occupational profile
sources.supports: Power engineers monitor alarms, gauges and instruments, keep a daily log of operation, maintenance and safety activities, start and stop boilers, isolate and lock out equipment for repair, troubleshoot failures and switch to manual control; shift work including nights, weekends and emergency overtime; an ABSA certificate is needed to supervise a power plant and assistants may work under a certified engineer. Publication year not shown; year is the access year.

sources.title: ISO Rules Part 200, Section 203.4 Delivery Requirements for Energy (effective 2023-03-31)
sources.supports: Pool participants deliver energy only under a dispatch or directive; must use dispatch protocols, personnel and software to detect and address errors; must start moving toward a dispatched MW level within 10 minutes; ramp time limits from the submitted ramp rate; an operational deviation of 20 minutes or longer requires an available capability or MW restatement no later than 20 minutes after it starts; exceptions for units synchronising or going off line at minimum stable generation, with a verbal ramp plan to the ISO updated for deviations over 30 minutes or 50 MW. Revision history: 2023 change was drafting alignment only; 2020-09-16 version in force during 2020-2022.

sources.title: Information Document ID 2012-009R Restatements (posted 2017-05-11)
sources.supports: Available capability restatements for an acceptable operational reason remove the highest-priced offer blocks from the merit order; price restatements are allowed up to two hours before the settlement interval without a reason; MW restatements only under defined operating conditions.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation 2021 Integrated Report (Form 6-K)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Adjusted availability 90.0 (2019), 90.7 (2020) and 86.6 percent (2021); Sundance 6, Keephills 2 and Keephills 3 converted to gas in Q1, Q2 and Q4 2021; planned conversion outages lowered 2021 availability; Alberta Gas production 8,691, 7,732 and 7,281 GWh in 2019-2021; power dispatched by AESO merit order; the company manages its offers internally and optimised production toward high-price periods in 2021. Only the first 100,000 characters of the filing were read.

sources.title: Fending off forced power plant outages
sources.supports: Cites NERC's 2020 State of Reliability (2019 fleet WEFOR 6.97 percent; gas outages spike in extreme winter weather) and NETL (August 2020, GADS data: boiler tube leaks cause more than half of coal-unit forced outages; balance of plant 15, steam turbine 13, generator 12, human error 4 percent; cycling stresses steam piping, headers and tubes) and an Intertek note that a base-load plant moving from 3-6 to 50 starts a year can see component failures within 2-6 years. Publication year not shown on the page as read.

assumptions: touch_min on crew steps (meeting, rounds, monitoring) is person-minutes summed over everyone on that step, so labour cost and the staffing check are right. The simulator adds every step's touch time in sequence, so its cycle time (about 2 to 3 days) is far longer than the real 12.5-hour shift in which the control room, field rounds and tests run at the same time; the concurrent_with fields mark this overlap.

One case is one plant-shift at one of two plant sites; the Keephills site runs two units and Sundance one, so a case holds on average 1.5 converted units for the 12 hours (converted_gas_unit occupied 720 to 1,440 minutes).

Crew size (one supervisor, about two control room operators and three to four field operators per plant-shift) and FTE on this process are tier C estimates for converted units; they are well below the organisation file headcounts, which fit the larger coal-era fleet.

Dispatches are received and acknowledged by the real-time desk (mkt-respond-dispatch) and passed to the plant; at plants with an ETS screen in the control room the operator may see them directly. Restatements during derates are shown here because they interrupt the shift, and are also counted in mkt-restate-offers.
Permit issue is in gas-issue-work-permits; only the field operator's isolation work during the shift is shown here.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage times 1.40).
The steps account for about 45 of the roughly 80 person-hours a crew of six to seven spends on a 12.5-hour shift; the rest is breaks, training, housekeeping and standby time not tied to a step.
Job requisitions to hr-recruit-hire are listed in the organisation file as an output of this process but are not a per-shift output; they are left out of interfaces.
